The crop in image pixels, with rotation, flipX and flipY.

The crop is a box in the image’s own pixels, with its rotation and flip. Pass it to `cropImage` to get a file you can upload. An image from another site needs CORS, or the browser won’t let the page read its pixels.

The cropper is a group named by `aria-label`. The selection and each handle are sliders that say the crop in words, like “300 by 300 pixels, at 50, 0”, and the zoom says its level, like “125%”. Those names are in English, so pass `aria-label` to each part to name it in your page’s language.
The edge or corner it resizes.

The grid only fades in while you drag, and not at all when motion is reduced. Handles get a larger hit area on touch screens, the page doesn’t scroll during a drag, and in forced colors mode the selection gets a system-colored border.
The image’s width over its height once it loads. The viewport takes it as its aspect ratio.
Turns the image a quarter clockwise, or back with Shift.
